case_title: GOTH FERRARI: THE $250M CRYPTO HEIST'S INSTRUMENT OF LAST RESORT

beats.label: hook
beats.text: When hackers couldn't trick their victims into handing over their crypto, they called Marlon Ferro. He'd break into your house and take it.

beats.label: setup
beats.text: Ferro, 20, was the so-called instrument of last resort for a 250 million dollar social engineering ring. When victims stored their crypto on hardware wallets, devices that can't be hacked remotely, the enterprise sent him in.

beats.label: escalation
beats.text: February 2024. Winnsboro, Texas. Ferro broke into a home and walked out with 100 bitcoin. More than 5 million dollars. July 2024. New Mexico. He staked out the house for days. When co-conspirators tracked the victim's iCloud and confirmed he was gone, Ferro smashed a window with a brick. The home camera caught him.

beats.label: resolution
beats.text: The stolen money bought Hermes Birkin bags, exotic cars up to 3.8 million dollars, nightclub tabs of half a million a night, and private jets. Ferro was arrested with two firearms and a fake ID. This month, a federal judge sentenced him to 78 months in prison, and 2.5 million in restitution.
